settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know: The hook events Hive knows Claude Code sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.

The top-level fields Hive knows Claude Code sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a Claude Code update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.preT: How long Claude Code waits for Hive's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Hive doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.time: How long Claude Code waits for Hive to take one of its hooks (a turn starting or ending, a notification). Hive answers at once; raise it only if Hive's log shows hooks timing out on a slow machine.
Claude Code's note in its transcript when its safety classifier stops a response, and the notice it adds for the model (#606). Wrong, Hive misses such stops: no shield on the agent's pane, and Performance doesn't count them.

Claude Code's question after a safeguard stop, whether to switch models, told by its open dialog's choices in the lines it wrote last. Hive shows the agent waiting for you, and why, while it is open; wrong, the agent shows only "Claude needs your permission".
settings.advanced.claude-code.signIn.sto: The error a StopFailure hook names when Claude Code's sign-in was refused (expired, revoked, an invalid key): Hive shows the agent signed out and offers to carry on once it's renewed (#309). Any other error ends the turn as failed.
settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine: The plan limits' field for the 5-hour window.

The top-level fields Hive knows Claude Code sends in its status line. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a status line with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
The status line's field with a subscription's limits (the 5-hour and weekly use the status bar shows). Wrong, Hive shows no plan limits for Claude Code.
A limit's field with the percentage used.
The plan limits' field for the weekly window.
settings.advanced.claude-code.trust.prom: Claude Code's question before a folder's first session. Hive shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.claude-code.turnScreen: Claude Code's line above its input when the last turn is done ("✻ Worked for 12s · done 16:52"). When Hive missed a turn's end, it takes this on screen to mean the agent is idle; wrong, it leaves such an agent's status unknown, with Mark idle.
settings.advanced.claudeFooter.desc: Claude Code's footer in the {mode} mode ("{footer}"). Hive reads an agent's permission mode from its footer (the mode found last on screen), and switches modes by pressing Shift+Tab until the footer shows the one wanted; wrong, Hive doesn't see the agent in {mode}, and can't switch to it without a restart.
settings.advanced.claudeFooter.title: Footer: {mode}
settings.advanced.codex.fullAccess.answe: How long Hive's switch to Full Access waits for you to answer Codex's own warning in its terminal. Meanwhile Hive types nothing into the agent; once it passes, Hive says Codex didn't confirm the switch, and still notices it later if you answer Yes.
Full Access warning: wait for your answer
settings.advanced.codex.fullAccess.warni: Codex's own warning after Full Access is picked in its /permissions menu, which you answer in its terminal. While it is on screen, Hive's switch to Full Access waits for your answer; if it doesn't match, Hive may say Codex didn't confirm the switch while the warning is still waiting.

How long Codex has, after Hive picks a preset in its /permissions menu before its first message, to show its own warning (Full Access). With no session file to read the switch back from, Hive takes the preset as switched once this passes with no warning; raise it if a slow machine draws the warning later.
Full Access warning: time to appear
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.knownEvent: The hook events Hive knows Codex sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.knownField: The top-level fields Hive knows Codex sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a Codex update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.preToolUse: How long Codex waits for Hive's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Hive doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.codex.hooks.timeoutSec: How long Codex waits for Hive to take one of its hooks. Codex itself holds the interrupt and session-end hooks to {most, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} at most. Hive approves its hooks for Codex itself, so a change needs no review in Codex.
settings.advanced.codex.mcp.toolTimeoutS: How long Codex lets one of Hive's tools run (its tool_timeout_sec for the hive server). Hive's waits stay a minute under it.
settings.advanced.codex.prompt.drawnSeco: How long Hive waits for Codex to show a line Hive typed (a message's notice, a wake) in its prompt before pressing Enter. Codex drops an Enter that it reads together with the line while it is busy, so Hive presses Enter once the line shows; if it doesn't show in time, Hive presses Enter anyway, and presses it again 10 seconds later if the line wasn't sent.
Typed line: wait to be drawn
settings.advanced.codex.queue.hint.desc: Codex's hint on the last line it draws while it is busy and queues what is typed. Hive waits for it to go before typing into Codex (a message, its /permissions menu at setup); wrong, what Hive types can be queued rather than run.
settings.advanced.codex.queue.hint.title: Screen: holding what was typed
settings.advanced.codex.rateLimits.field: The field of Codex's token counts with a subscription's limits. Wrong, Hive shows no plan limits for Codex.
settings.advanced.codex.rateLimits.usedP: A limit's field with the percentage used.
settings.advanced.codex.rateLimits.windo: A limit's field with its window in minutes (300 is the 5-hour limit, 10080 the weekly one).
settings.advanced.codex.ready.placeholde: The text Codex's empty input shows. Codex only says it has started with the first prompt, so Hive takes this text on screen to mean it is ready, and an input line showing only this to mean it is idle.
settings.advanced.codex.signIn.expired.d: A turn's error, in Codex's session file, that means its sign-in was refused or has expired, when Codex doesn't mark the error itself (#309).
settings.advanced.codex.title.items.desc: What Hive asks Codex to put in its terminal title (tui.terminal_title): its activity, which shows the busy spinner and "Action Required", and the project's name. Without activity, Hive can't tell from the title that Codex is working or needs you.
settings.advanced.codex.trust.prompt.des: Codex's question before a folder's first session (in a Git repository). Hive shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.codex.turnScreen.worki: Codex's Working line, drawn only while a turn runs. When Hive missed a turn's start or end, it takes this on screen to mean the agent is working; wrong, it can take a working agent for idle.
settings.advanced.codexPermissions.desc: The label Codex's /permissions menu shows for its {label} preset. Hive types the number beside it to give an agent the {mode} mode; wrong, Hive can't find it, and says so rather than choosing another.
settings.advanced.codexPermissions.title: /permissions menu: {label}
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.con: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the conversation's tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.sum: The field of a compaction's end, in Copilot's session file, with the summary it carries on from: the Sessions tab shows it with the compaction.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.sys: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the system prompt's tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.too: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the tool definitions' tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.exit.graceSeco: When Hive stops Copilot (Stop, Restart, closing a project or quitting), how long it gives Copilot to exit by itself after its Ctrl+C before killing it. Copilot writes the session's token totals only as it exits by itself: one killed first loses them. It took up to {took, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} on a busy machine (#716); quitting Hive or closing a workspace waits up to this long, and a second more, for a Copilot that hangs.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.knownEve: The hook events Hive knows GitHub Copilot sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.knownFie: The top-level fields Hive knows GitHub Copilot sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a GitHub Copilot update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.preToolU: How long Copilot waits for Hive's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Hive doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.timeoutS: How long Copilot waits for Hive to take one of its hooks.
settings.advanced.copilot.mouse.rightCli: Right-click in a Copilot pane is Hive's, as in every pane: it copies the terminal's selection (Shift+drag), or pastes. Turned on, Hive passes right-clicks to Copilot instead, which copies its own selection (a drag) with them, as its footer says.
settings.advanced.copilot.ready.footer.d: Copilot only says it has started with the first prompt, so Hive takes its footer on screen to mean it is ready.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorMe: A session error's message, in Copilot's session file, that means its sign-in was refused, when its type doesn't say so.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorTy: A session error's type, in Copilot's session file, that means its sign-in was refused or is missing (#309): Hive shows the agent signed out.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.hookMes: The message of Copilot's ErrorOccurred hook that means a model call was refused for the sign-in: the turn ends signed out. Another error that ends the turn ends it as failed.
settings.advanced.copilot.trust.prompt.d: Copilot's question before a folder's first session. Hive shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.copilotFooter.desc: Copilot's footer in the {mode} mode ("{footer}"){shared, select, yes {, which Ask and Accept edits share (Hive tells them apart by the mode the session started in)} other {}}. Hive reads an agent's mode from its footer (the mode found last on screen), and switches modes by pressing Shift+Tab until the footer shows the one wanted; wrong, Hive doesn't see the agent in that mode, and can't switch to it without a restart.
settings.advanced.copilotFooter.title: Footer: {mode}
settings.advanced.data.tip: Project settings live in each project's .hive folder; workspace settings in the workspace .hive folder.
settings.advanced.data.title: Settings file
settings.advanced.error.field: {title} takes a field name: letters, digits and _ (not starting with a digit).
settings.advanced.error.list: {title} takes 1 to 10 names (letters, digits, - and _), as a list or separated by commas.
settings.advanced.error.matchesAll: {title} would match anything (it matches empty text).
settings.advanced.error.number: {title} takes a whole number from {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.error.oneLine: {title} takes one line of at most {most} characters.
settings.advanced.hive.agents.perProject: How many agents a project can have (#562): {usual} unless you need more, up to {most}. Each agent runs its own copy of its CLI, so more agents take more memory, and they all share your plans' usage limits. Lowering it removes no agents: a project with more just can't add another. Templates and the Agent API keep to it too.
Show the text in the developer console: prompts, replies, commands and tools' arguments, under a banner saying it is unredacted, and start each recording with its text box ticked. Tokens, API keys and sign-in details stay masked whatever this says; agents' hive_console stays redacted, and a recording with text is never attached to Copy Diagnostics.
Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text
settings.advanced.hive.disableHardwareAc: Draw Hive without the graphics card, for a graphics driver that leaves Hive's window blank, flickering or crashing. Terminals then draw without WebGL. Takes effect when Hive restarts; to start once without it, run Hive with --disable-gpu.
settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL: When Hive's main process nears its memory limit, it writes a snapshot of its memory to the heap folder in Hive's profile before it closes, to find out what filled it. A snapshot can be several gigabytes, holds whatever Hive had in memory (card text, transcripts, possibly tokens) and stays on this PC; Hive keeps the newest two. Takes effect when Hive restarts.
Save a memory snapshot if Hive is about to run out of memory
How long the hive MCP server waits for Hive to answer one of its tools (a wait's own time comes on top). Raise it when a slow or very busy machine makes hive tools fail with "Hive didn't reply within 300 s" (#371).
settings.advanced.hive.progress.lanesSho: How many card-loop lanes the Progress panel shows before its lanes scroll, until you drag the section's top edge (the drag is kept per workspace). A workspace that runs many lanes at once can set its own.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec: How long a capture waits after its trigger before it is saved, so it holds what followed too: what the CLI did next.
Flight recorder: wait after a trigger
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.keep.des: How many captures Hive keeps in its console-recordings folder: past it, the oldest go. Recordings you made in the developer console are never removed.
How long after a capture the same trigger waits before it captures the same agent again, so something that keeps happening saves one capture, not many.
Flight recorder: one capture per trigger and agent every
Save a capture when an agent's developer console event has a name or summary this regular expression finds (case-insensitive). The default, (?!), never finds anything: it is off.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.safeguar: Save a capture when a model's safeguards stop a response or switch the model: the agent's newest developer console events, redacted, in Hive's console-recordings folder, with a notice. With any flight recorder trigger on, Hive keeps each agent's newest developer console events in memory (redacted), whether a console is open or not.
Save a capture when an agent working on a turn goes silent past its limit, so Hive can't tell what it is doing.
Flight recorder: capture an agent gone silent
Save a capture when a CLI sends a hook or a status line with a field Hive doesn't know: often the first sign that a CLI update changed something.
Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI
Save a capture when an agent starts on a version of its CLI other than the one the last agent of that CLI started on.
Flight recorder: capture a CLI version change
settings.advanced.hive.showDeveloperFeat: Show Help → Developer Console (Ctrl+Alt+J): what each CLI sends Hive, next to what Hive made of it.
settings.advanced.hive.wait.agentsMaxSec: The longest hive_wait_for_agents waits for agents to finish before it answers. Kept a minute below Codex's hive tool timeout, as card waits are.
settings.advanced.hive.wait.cardMaxSecon: The longest an agent's hive_wait_for_tasks call (without wake) waits before it answers. It has to stay under the CLIs' own tool timeouts, so Hive keeps it a minute below Codex's hive tool timeout whatever is set here.
settings.advanced.logs.desc: Open the folder containing Hive's log files.
settings.advanced.logs.title: Logs
settings.advanced.miss.field: {cli} {version} sent no field "{field}" here (it sent {fields}). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.list: {cli} {version} sent {missing}, which this list doesn't have (it sent {fields}). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.text: It doesn't find what {cli} {version} showed ("{shown}"). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.reset.desc: Restore every setting in Settings to its default, the advanced settings in advanced.json too. Workspaces and projects, and a workspace's own advanced values, are not affected.
settings.advanced.reset.tip: Recent workspaces and window position are kept.
settings.advanced.reset.title: Reset all settings
For power users and for developing Hive. The console opens in a window of its own; Hive captures a source only while it is open on it, redacted. Turning this off closes it.
settings.advanced.takes.number: A whole number of {unit, select, s {seconds} lanes {lanes} agents {agents} other {units}}, {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.values.desc: Details Hive relies on that a CLI update can break (the text of its prompts, the fields it sends), and timeouts and limits for power users. Change one only when something doesn't work, or Hive's notes on a CLI update say to.
settings.advanced.values.tip: Each shows its default beside it once changed, and Reset puts the default back. A value that isn't valid is ignored, with a warning, and the default used. They are kept in advanced.json in your Hive profile, which you can also edit by hand (Open advanced.json): Hive reads it again when it changes. A value for a CLI records the CLI version it was made for, and is flagged when another version is installed. Some take a workspace's own value too.
settings.advanced.values.title: Advanced settings
settings.advancedList.alsoSetting: Hive's setting {key}, kept in advanced.json too.
settings.advancedList.cliVersion: It is {cli}'s: a change records the version it was made for.
settings.advancedList.fileError: {problem} Hive keeps using the values it read before; fix the file to change them.
settings.advancedList.label: {group}: {title}
settings.advancedList.madeFor: Made for {cli} {version}; {installed} is installed now. Check it still works, then keep it for {installed}.
settings.advancedList.notValid: Not valid, so Hive uses the default: {problem}
settings.advancedList.unknown: advanced.json also names {ids}, which this Hive doesn't know (a typo, or a newer Hive's): kept in the file, not used.
settings.advancedRow.tip: {takes} null (or Reset) goes back to Hive's default.{cli, select, yes { It is {group}'s: an override records the version it was made for, and is flagged when another version is installed.{tried, select, yes { Hive tries it on what the CLI was recorded sending, and says when it doesn't find that.} other {}}} other {}}
settings.advancedRow.title: {group}: {title}
settings.advancedRow.workspaceDesc: This workspace's own value; empty uses Settings → Advanced's. {desc}
settings.agentApi.allowSessionInput.conf: Any program with the API token will be able to type commands into running sessions.
settings.agentApi.allowSessionInput.desc: Let API clients type into running sessions (POST /v1/projects/'{'name'}'/input).
settings.agentApi.allowSessionInput.tip: Powerful: an agent in one project could drive another project's session. Keep off unless you need orchestration.
settings.agentApi.devConsole.desc: Give agents and the Hive Assistant a read-only hive tool for the developer console: what their CLI sends Hive, next to what Hive made of it.
settings.agentApi.devConsole.tip: Each agent reads only its own sessions; the Assistant reads its workspace's agents and Hive's own events. Hive captures only while the developer console is open on a source (reading starts nothing), and what it captures is redacted: no prompt or reply text, commands, tokens or sign-in details. Running sessions get the tool after a restart.
settings.agentApi.devConsole.title: Let agents read the developer console
settings.agentApi.enabled.desc: Run a local HTTP API that agents and scripts can use to talk to Hive.
settings.agentApi.enabled.tip: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only and requires the bearer token below. See Help → Agent API Reference. Turned off, the port still answers the Hive Assistant alone (it has its own token, and Settings → Assistant → Control decides what it may do).
settings.agentApi.enabled.title: Enable Agent API
settings.agentApi.port.desc: Local port for the Agent API.
settings.agentApi.port.tip: Change this if the port is used by another program.
settings.agentApi.port.title: Port
settings.agentApi.provideHiveMcp.desc: Add the built-in "hive" MCP server to every session.
settings.agentApi.provideHiveMcp.tip: Gives agents tools for shared notes, handovers, project status and notifications.
settings.agentApi.provideHiveMcp.title: Provide Hive tools to sessions
settings.agentApi.status.tip: Whether the Agent API is listening.
settings.agentApi.status.title: Status
settings.agentApi.token.desc: Bearer token required by the Agent API.
settings.agentApi.token.tip: Stored in %APPDATA%\Hive\agent-api.json. Sessions receive it automatically as HIVE_API_TOKEN.
settings.agentApi.token.title: Access token
settings.agentApi.viewers.desc: Read-only tokens for apps that show Hive, such as Apiary: they can read everything and follow its events, and change nothing.
settings.agentApi.viewers.tip: Name each one for its app. Stored in %APPDATA%\Hive\agent-api-viewers.json. Revoking one cuts its app off at once. Apps find a running Hive by %APPDATA%\Hive\agent-api-discovery.json (the address, no token).
settings.agentApi.viewers.title: Viewer tokens
settings.agents.backgroundTaskMinutes.de: Minutes an agent waits on a background task it started (such as a test run) before Hive counts it as finished anyway.
settings.agents.backgroundTaskMinutes.ti: An agent that ends its turn while a task it started is still running shows as waiting on background tasks, not finished: Claude Code carries on by itself when the task ends. Hive can't tell a test run from something that never ends, such as a dev server, so it stops counting a task after this long (a Monitor also when it expires). Codex isn't told when its background terminals end, so they are only counted and shown. {min, number} to {max, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
Count background tasks for up to
settings.agents.fileLocks.desc: What happens when an agent tries to edit a file another agent in the same folder is editing.
settings.agents.fileLocks.tip: An agent claims a file when it edits it and releases it when its turn ends (or after 15 minutes). Agents in their own worktrees never collide. Edits made through shell commands are not covered.
settings.agents.fileLocks.title: File locks
settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.desc: What Hive does with processes an agent started that are still running when it stops, such as a preview server or a tail -f.
settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.tip: Hive follows every process an agent's session starts, however it was started. Ask: a notification lists them and offers to end them; the agent's pane header shows them until they end or you decide. End them: Hive ends them as the agent stops. Hive never ends a process the agent didn't start, and asks about the ones still running when you quit.
settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.title: Processes left running
settings.agents.mergeStyle.desc: How a worktree agent's branch is merged back, unless you choose otherwise in the Merge dialog.
settings.agents.mergeStyle.tip: Merge keeps the agent's commits and their messages, plus a merge commit: right for an agent that keeps its worktree for task after task. Squash makes one commit with everything the agent did.
settings.agents.mergeStyle.title: Default merge style
settings.agents.worktreeCopy.desc: Git-ignored files copied from the project folder into each new worktree, comma separated (e.g. .env*, config/local.json).
settings.agents.worktreeCopy.tip: A new worktree only gets the files git tracks. Patterns without a slash match a file or folder name anywhere; with a slash they match a path from the project root. Projects can set their own list and a setup command (e.g. npm install) in Project Settings → Agents & Worktrees.
settings.agents.worktreeCopy.title: Copy into new worktrees
settings.appearance.terminalFontFamily.d: Font family for session terminals (CSS font list).
settings.appearance.terminalFontFamily.t: Monospace fonts work best. Cascadia Code ships with Windows Terminal; Nerd Fonts add extra glyphs.
settings.appearance.terminalFontSize.des: Font size for session terminals, in pixels.
settings.appearance.terminalScrollback.d: Lines kept in each terminal for scrolling back.
settings.appearance.terminalScrollback.t: Higher values use more memory per running session.
settings.appearance.theme.tip: System follows your Windows light/dark setting.
settings.appearance.theme.title: Theme
settings.appearance.uiFontSize.desc: Font size for menus, lists and panels, in pixels.
settings.appearance.uiFontSize.tip: View → Zoom In and Zoom Out scale everything, including the terminal.
settings.appearance.uiFontSize.title: Interface font size
settings.assistant.changeSettings.desc: Let the Assistant change Hive's settings when you ask it to, in every workspace. Whatever this says, it can read and explain them.
settings.assistant.changeSettings.tip: It suggests a setting first and changes one only when you agree. Each change is listed in its panel with the old and new value and a Revert button, and counts towards its 30 changes per message. It can never change its own Control, permission modes, the Agent API or what Hive runs (CLI paths, extra arguments, setup commands): it tells you where to change those. A running Assistant takes a change after a restart.
settings.assistant.changeSettings.title: Change settings
Context size, in tokens, at which the Assistant's Compact button and the context count in its footer turn orange. Never: they never do.

The Assistant usually runs a bigger context than your agents, so it has its own threshold (your agents' is Settings → Sessions → Suggest compacting above). Compacting summarises the conversation so every later message is cheaper; the full history stays in the transcript.
settings.assistant.control.desc: What the Assistant may do beyond looking and advising, in every workspace.
settings.assistant.control.tip: It never removes agents, discards worktrees or deletes projects, never types into an agent that is working, asking you something or that you just typed in (see Pause after you type), and makes at most 30 changes per message. What it does is listed in its panel. A running Assistant takes a change after a restart.
settings.assistant.control.tip.agents: Control agents: it can also add agents, change their settings, start and stop them, and give idle ones tasks, when you ask it to. Stopping a busy agent asks you first.
settings.assistant.control.tip.look: Look and advise: it reads and suggests, and you act.
settings.assistant.control.tip.projects: Control agents and create projects: also new projects.
settings.assistant.control.title: Control
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.desc: Once you press Enter in the terminal (you sent what you typed), the Assistant may type there at once.
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.tip: Turn this off if you often type a line and then keep writing (e.g. answering a question, then adding more).
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.title: Enter ends the pause
settings.assistant.journal.desc: The Assistant keeps a journal in this workspace: decisions, plans, events and what it learned, recalled a few lines at a time instead of reading a long handover. Hive adds facts: lanes, merges, unexpected closes.
settings.assistant.journal.tip: For this workspace. Turning it off keeps the entries; Delete Journal… removes them. The Assistant's journal tools follow a change at its next start; it is told at once.
settings.assistant.journal.title: Journal
settings.assistant.panelSide.desc: Which side of the window the Assistant's panel is on, in every workspace.
settings.assistant.panelSide.tip: On the left it sits between the project list and your work, which keeps it clear of Windows notifications and other windows at the bottom right. View → Move Assistant Panel… and the panel's ⋯ menu switch it too.
settings.assistant.panelSide.title: Panel side
settings.assistant.persona.desc: How the Assistant works in a new conversation (Coordinator, Planner, QA triager, Release manager, or your own), unless a workspace chooses another.
settings.assistant.persona.tip: Modes are Markdown files in each workspace (.hive/personas): edit them, or add your own, in the Hive Assistant view (the robot on the left). The panel switches mode at once, keeping the conversation.
settings.assistant.persona.title: Default mode
settings.assistant.provider.desc: The coding agent the Assistant runs, unless a workspace chooses another.
settings.assistant.provider.tip: The Assistant is independent of your project agents: a Codex Assistant can look after Claude Code agents, and the other way round.
settings.assistant.provider.title: Provider
settings.assistant.tellReplies.desc: The Assistant's watch on an agent or its card hears the first line of what you send that agent from its pane.
settings.assistant.tellReplies.tip: So it knows what you told the agent (an answer, a decision) without asking you again, and can record a decision on the card. Only the first line, only to the Assistant of the same workspace, and only when it is watching that agent or its card.
settings.assistant.tellReplies.title: Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent
settings.assistant.typingPause.desc: Seconds after you type in an agent's terminal before the Assistant may type there (give it a task or hand its work over).
settings.assistant.typingPause.tip: The Assistant types a task by clearing the agent's input line (Ctrl+U) and entering it, which would wipe or mix with something you were writing. During the pause it asks you instead.
settings.assistant.typingPause.title: Pause after you type
settings.assistant.withProvider.desc: The model, effort, permission mode{context, select, yes {, context} other {}} and extra arguments when the Assistant runs {provider}. Default follows {provider}'s own settings, except the mode: {mode}, where {provider} approves safe actions itself and only asks about risky ones.
settings.assistant.withProvider.tip: By default it uses the same model and effort as your agents. A lighter model or low effort saves tokens but makes it careless (for example, saying it will check on an agent later and never doing so). Its default mode is the one your agents default to, so it rarely asks. Hive's own tools never ask: what they may do is set by Control above.
settings.assistant.withProvider.title: With {provider}
settings.assistantProvider.effort.desc: Its reasoning effort with {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider} → Default effort.
settings.assistantProvider.effort.title: Effort
settings.assistantProvider.extraArgs.des: Additional {cli} command-line arguments when the Assistant runs {provider}.
settings.assistantProvider.model.desc: The model when the Assistant runs {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider} → Default model.
settings.assistantProvider.model.title: Model
settings.assistantProvider.permissionMod: Its permission mode with {provider}. Empty is {mode}, where {provider} approves safe actions itself and only asks about risky ones.
settings.assistantProvider.use200kContex: A 200K-token context window for it with {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider}.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.desc: Days a card stays in Done before Hive archives it.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.tip: Counted from when the card last went into Done (or was brought back from the archive), not from its last change. An archived card is kept: the board's Archived list shows it, and you can bring it back. Hive checks when a workspace opens and every hour.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.title: Archive Done cards after
settings.board.colors.desc: Pick the colour of each column.
settings.board.colors.tip: The tint on cards is a light mix of the colour with the theme, so it works in light and dark themes. Reset puts back the default.
settings.board.colors.title: Column colours
settings.board.columnColors.desc: Give each column's heading its colour and tint its cards with it.
settings.board.columnColors.tip: A card takes the colour of the column it is in. Blocked, stalled and finished cards keep their red, amber and green edge, and their text, over the tint.
settings.board.columnColors.title: Colour columns
settings.fallback.levelsPerModel: {source}: each model offers its own levels; this list names them and is used for models it doesn't describe.
settings.fallback.levelsUsed: Used now: {provider} hasn't reported per-model levels.
settings.fallback.name: Name
settings.fallback.showLevels: Show the list ({n, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}})
settings.fallback.showModels: Show the list ({n, plural, one {# model} other {# models}})
settings.general.closeToTray.desc: Closing the window keeps Hive running in the system tray so sessions continue.
settings.general.closeToTray.tip: When off, closing the window quits Hive (asking first if sessions are running). Use File → Exit or the tray menu to quit.
settings.general.closeToTray.title: Close to tray
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.desc: When to ask before quitting stops running sessions.
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.tip: Quitting stops every running session. Their conversations are kept and can be resumed, so by default Hive only asks when an agent is in the middle of something (working, or waiting for your answer).
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.title: Confirm before quitting
settings.general.dateFormat.desc: How dates show in Hive: sessions named by when they started, the session lists and their tooltips, exports.
settings.general.dateFormat.tip: System uses your Windows language's short date. Names you give sessions stay as you typed them: only the automatic ones (when a session started) follow this. How long ago something happened ("2 hours ago") stays, with the date on hover.
settings.general.dateFormat.title: Date format
settings.general.keepAwake.desc: Stop Windows from sleeping while an agent is working or waiting on background tasks, so it doesn't stop mid-task.
settings.general.keepAwake.tip: Hive lets the PC sleep again as soon as no agent is working. The screen can still turn off and lock. On a laptop, "When plugged in" lets it sleep on battery.
settings.general.keepAwake.title: Keep the PC awake while agents work
settings.general.launchAtLogin.desc: Start Hive automatically when you sign in to Windows.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.tip: Hive starts hidden in the tray when launched at login.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.title: Launch at login
settings.general.minimizeToTray.desc: Minimising hides Hive to the system tray instead of the taskbar.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.tip: Click the tray icon to bring Hive back.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.title: Minimise to tray
settings.general.progressCommands.desc: Agents run tests, builds and other commands that take more than about 30 seconds through hive-progress without being asked, so they show in the panel. Off: only when you ask.
settings.general.progressCommands.disabl: Turn on the Progress panel to use this.
settings.general.progressCommands.tip: hive-progress runs the command unchanged (same output and exit code). Hive's session guidance tells agents to use it, so a change applies to agents started or restarted afterwards. With the Progress panel off, agents aren't told to use it either.
settings.general.progressCommands.title: Agents show long commands in the Progress panel
settings.general.progressPanel.desc: Show long runs agents report, such as tests and builds: how far along each is and the time left, in a panel on the right and on the taskbar button.
settings.general.progressPanel.tip: Folded, the panel is a strip with a small bar per run; click it, or use Toggle Progress Panel in the command palette. Off hides the panel, the strip and the taskbar progress; agents can still report, and Hive ignores it.
settings.general.progressPanel.title: Progress panel
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.des: Open the workspace you used last when Hive starts.
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.tip: Sessions are never resumed automatically — only the workspace is reopened.
settings.general.showTips.desc: One tip a day about something Hive can do, and a tip at the moments one helps.
settings.general.showTips.tip: Tips show in a small card in the bottom corner and never get in the way. Help → Tips… lists them all, whether this is on or off.
settings.general.showTips.title: Show a tip when Hive starts
settings.general.startMinimized.desc: Start Hive hidden in the system tray.
settings.general.startMinimized.title: Start in tray
settings.general.timeFormat.desc: How times show with the dates.
settings.general.timeFormat.tip: Applies wherever Hive shows a time, such as a session that started today or the time a screenshot was pasted.
settings.general.timeFormat.title: Time format
settings.general.userName.desc: How Hive names you to the Hive Assistant when it tells it you replied to an agent ("Darren replied to B1 on #399").
settings.general.userName.tip: It goes into the Assistant's conversation, so use whatever form you like it to see. Empty uses "User".
settings.general.userName.title: Your name
settings.journal.deleteMessage: All {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} of this workspace go to the Recycle Bin. The Assistant starts again with an empty journal.
settings.journal.local: Kept on this computer only, in .hive/assistant/journal.db, and never sent anywhere.
settings.journal.mb: MB (past it, the oldest everyday entries go first)
settings.journal.noWorkspace: Open a workspace to set its Assistant's journal.
settings.journal.offKeeps: Off, nothing is written and the Assistant's journal tools go at its next start; the entries are kept.
settings.journal.size: Now {size}, {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}.
settings.keybindings.editor.desc: Click the pencil (or double-click a shortcut), then press the new keys. Wait a moment after the first combination, or press a second one for a chord such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S.
settings.keybindings.editor.tip: Shortcuts need Ctrl or Alt (or are F-keys). Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Shift+Tab stay with editing and the agents' terminals. Some keys go to the agent while its terminal has focus (for Claude Code: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+G).
settings.keybindings.editor.title: Shortcuts
settings.keys.chordNext: then another key for a chord…
settings.keys.inUseDetail: When two commands share a shortcut, the first one listed that is available runs. Change the other one to avoid surprises.
settings.keys.inUseMessage: {keys} is used by {commands}. Use it here too?
settings.keys.projectNote: Changes here apply while {project} is selected, over the global shortcuts. Other commands are set in Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts.
settings.keys.resetAllGlobal: {n, plural, one {Return # changed shortcut to the defaults.} other {Return # changed shortcuts to the defaults.}}
settings.keys.resetAllProject: {n, plural, one {Remove {project}'s shortcut change; it uses the global shortcuts again.} other {Remove {project}'s # shortcut changes; it uses the global shortcuts again.}}
settings.keys.terminalKey: While an agent's terminal has focus this key goes to the agent, so the shortcut only works elsewhere.
settings.metrics.resetDetail: The history starts again from now.
settings.metrics.resetFailed: Could not reset the performance metrics
settings.metrics.resetMessage: Clear this workspace's recorded performance metrics?
settings.notifications.bannerPosition.de: Where banners show in the window.
settings.notifications.bannerPosition.ti: Several stack, the newest nearest the edge.
settings.notifications.bannerScope.desc: Which notices the window you are using shows as banners.
settings.notifications.bannerScope.tip: Clicking a banner from another window brings that window up. A notice left out shows nothing, but still counts on its own window's taskbar button and in its inbox.
settings.notifications.bannerScope.title: Show banners for
settings.notifications.bannerSeconds.des: How long a banner for a finished agent, or another notice, stays.
settings.notifications.bannerSeconds.tip: It stays while the pointer is on it.
settings.notifications.chimeEnabled.desc: Play a sound when an agent finishes or needs your input.
settings.notifications.chimeEnabled.tip: Projects can override this in their settings.
settings.notifications.chimeSound.tip: Sounds are synthesised by Hive — no audio files needed.
settings.notifications.chimeSound.title: Chime sound
settings.notifications.chimeVolume.title: Chime volume
settings.notifications.desktopNotificati: Tell you when an agent finishes or needs input: in Hive while you use it, else with a Windows notification.
Clicking one shows its project. Off, nothing is shown either way; the chime and the taskbar have settings of their own.
settings.notifications.flashOnWaiting.de: When an agent starts waiting for your answer while Hive is in the background.
settings.notifications.flashOnWaiting.ti: It stops when you switch to the window. Finishing agents never flash it.
Flash the taskbar button when an agent needs input
Notify when a session completes its task.
Triggered when the agent's turn ends (its Stop hook), or for an agent waiting on background tasks it started, when they have ended.
settings.notifications.notifyOnWaiting.d: Notify when a session is waiting for permission or input.
settings.notifications.notifyOnWaiting.t: Triggered by the agent's permission prompts and questions.
settings.notifications.taskbarCount.desc: A badge on Hive's taskbar button, and the window title, show how many agents need you.
settings.notifications.taskbarCount.tip: The same count as the status bar: agents waiting for your input, and those that finished while you were not looking. Each window shows its own workspace.
settings.notifications.taskbarCount.titl: Show a count on the taskbar button
settings.notifications.waitingBannerStay: Until you click or dismiss it, or answer the agent. Off, they close like the others.
Answering the agent anywhere (its terminal, another window) closes its banner.
Banners for an agent waiting for you stay until handled
settings.notifications.whileFocused.desc: What to show while you are using a Hive window. With Hive in the background, a Windows notification.
settings.notifications.whileFocused.tip: Show in Hive: a banner in the window you are using, where Windows notifications would cover the Assistant. The chime still plays either way.
settings.prices.checked: Hive's starting prices, checked {checked}: edit them if they are out of date.
settings.prices.newPlaceholder: Model ID, e.g. a new model
settings.prices.noReports: {provider} doesn't report costs, so Hive estimates them from these prices. Check them against <link>{company}'s pricing</link>.
settings.prices.unlistedTip: {provider} doesn't list this model now; its price stays for older sessions.
settings.project.agents.desc: Up to 12 agents can work on the project at once (up to 24 with Settings → Advanced → Agents per project), each in the project folder or its own worktree. Agents without their own settings use this project's.
settings.project.agents.title: Agents
settings.project.chime.desc: Play a sound when an agent in this project finishes or needs input.
settings.project.chime.title: Completion chime
settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.de: Context size (tokens) at which Compact is highlighted for this project. Empty inherits Settings → Sessions → Suggest compacting above.
settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.ti: Only changes when the Compact button turns orange; compacting is always available once the agent has finished.
settings.project.defaultProvider.desc: The provider Add Agent uses for this project's new agents (the dialog can choose another). Inherit uses Settings → Providers → Default provider.
settings.project.defaultProvider.tip: Each agent keeps the provider it was given; change it in the agent’s settings.
settings.project.defaultProvider.title: Default provider
settings.project.fileLocks.desc: What happens when an agent tries to edit a file another agent in this project's folder is editing. Inherit uses Settings → Agents & Worktrees → File locks.
settings.project.fileLocks.tip: Applies to agents sharing a folder (agents in their own worktrees never collide). An agent claims a file when it edits it and releases it when its turn ends. Edits made through shell commands are not covered.
settings.project.fileLocks.title: File locks
settings.project.keybindings.desc: Change one to give this project its own; Reset returns it to the global shortcut. Stored in the project’s .hive folder, which is not committed.
settings.project.keybindings.title: Shortcuts
settings.project.loopRounds.desc: How many rounds a card gets in this project's card loops before its agents stop and ask you, when you don't say. Empty inherits Settings → Workspace → Card loop rounds.
settings.project.loopRounds.tip: Saying "rounds: 5" when you start a loop still wins.
settings.project.loopRounds.title: Rounds
settings.project.loopWaitHours.desc: How many hours an agent in this project's card loops waits with no change before it tells you, when you don't say. Empty inherits Settings → Workspace → Card loop wait.
settings.project.loopWaitHours.tip: Saying "wait: 2h" when you start a loop still wins. Up to a day.
settings.project.loopWaitHours.title: Wait (hours)
settings.project.loopWakes.desc: When a card with a reviewer arrives in Review, Hive wakes the reviewer; when the review gives its verdict, Hive wakes the card's builder. Off: only the agents' own card watches wake them.
settings.project.loopWakes.tip: A card's reviewer is the reviewer of a lane with the card, else the agent that last reviewed it: cards nobody reviews never wake anyone. An agent is only woken while it is idle, never by its own change, and not when its own card watch already tells it.
settings.project.loopWakes.title: Wake reviewers and builders
settings.project.metadata.desc: Stored in the project's .hive/project.json (excluded from git). Changes apply to new sessions; restart a running session to apply them.
settings.project.metadata.title: Settings file
settings.project.reset.desc: Everything on this page goes back to Inherit. Agents, and skill and MCP opt-outs, are kept.
settings.project.reset.title: Reset project settings
settings.project.storage.desc: Measured in the background; Refresh measures again. The coding agents’ own transcripts (in ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.copilot) aren’t counted, and Clean Up… and Purge… never touch them.
settings.project.storage.title: What Hive keeps
settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.desc: Size, in MB, at which a running conversation's transcript is flagged for this project. Empty inherits Settings → Sessions → Warn when a transcript is over.
settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.tip: A long conversation slows down the CLI and Hive; handing the work over to a new conversation makes it short again.
settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.title: Warn when a transcript is over
settings.project.worktreeCopy.desc: Git-ignored files to copy from the project folder into a new worktree, such as .env files. One pattern per line; empty inherits Settings → Agents & Worktrees → Copy into new worktrees.
settings.project.worktreeCopy.tip: A new worktree only gets the files git tracks. Patterns without a slash match a file or folder name anywhere (e.g. .env*); with a slash they match a path from the project root (e.g. config/local.json). Large folders such as node_modules are better recreated by the setup command.
settings.project.worktreeCopy.title: Copy into new worktrees
settings.project.worktreeSetup.desc: Runs in a new worktree before its agent's first session, e.g. npm install. Its output shows in the agent's pane.
settings.project.worktreeSetup.tip: Runs with cmd.exe in the worktree folder. If it fails, the pane offers to retry or to start the agent without it.
settings.project.worktreeSetup.title: Setup command
settings.projectProvider.effort.desc: How much reasoning effort the model uses. Higher is more thorough but slower and uses more tokens.
settings.projectProvider.effort.tip: Passed to {provider} when a session starts. Inherit uses Settings → {provider} → Default effort.
settings.projectProvider.effort.title: Effort
settings.projectProvider.extraArgs.desc: Additional {cli} command-line arguments for this project, added after the global ones.
settings.projectProvider.extraArgs.tip: Split like a command line; quote arguments with spaces.
settings.projectProvider.extraArgs.title: Extra arguments
settings.projectProvider.model.desc: Model for this project's {provider} agents. Inherit uses Settings → {provider} → Default model.
settings.projectProvider.model.tip: Passed to {provider} when a session starts. Agents can choose their own.
settings.projectProvider.model.title: Model
You can still switch modes inside a running session with Shift+Tab.
The mode this project's {provider} sessions start in. Inherit uses Settings → {provider} → Default permission mode.
A 200K-token context window for this project's {provider} agents instead of the model's 1M one. Inherit uses Settings → {provider}.
Applies to sessions started afterwards. Agents can choose for themselves.
settings.projectSection.advanced.desc: Where the settings are stored, and resetting them.
settings.projectSection.advanced.label: Advanced
settings.projectSection.agents.desc: The project’s agents and their providers, file locks between them, and how new worktrees are set up.
settings.projectSection.agents.label: Agents & Worktrees
settings.projectSection.keys.desc: Shortcuts for project and session commands while this project is selected, over the global ones.
settings.projectSection.keys.label: Keyboard Shortcuts
settings.projectSection.loops.desc: How Hive helps agents that work through cards as builder and reviewer in this project.
settings.projectSection.loops.label: Card loops
settings.projectSection.provider.desc: Model, effort and permissions for this project’s {provider} agents. Agents can override these for themselves.
settings.projectSection.sessions.desc: Compacting and notifications for this project.
settings.projectSection.sessions.label: Sessions
settings.projectSection.storage.desc: What Hive keeps for this project: transcript backups, archived sessions, attachments and the agents’ worktrees. Clean Up… moves old backups and attachments to the Recycle Bin; Purge… removes everything Hive keeps for its sessions.
settings.projectSection.storage.label: Storage
settings.provider.allowBackgroundSession: Let {provider}'s agent view move a session into its own background service. Applies to sessions started afterwards.

Off by default. In {provider}, pressing ← on an empty prompt (easy to do while moving through text) opens its agent view and moves the session into the background. Hive can then no longer see it or stop it: Stop only closes the terminal, the session keeps running, and resuming it fails until it is stopped with "{cli} stop".
settings.provider.checkUpdatesOnLaunch.d: Compare the installed version with the latest release when Hive starts.
settings.provider.checkUpdatesOnLaunch.t: Hive never updates {provider} without asking. Standalone installs may also update themselves.
settings.provider.costSource.desc: Where a session's API-equivalent cost comes from: {provider}'s own report, or your prices in the table below.
settings.provider.costSource.tip: {provider}'s reported cost follows its own price table and updates with the CLI; Hive never recomputes it, even when that table lags a price change. Choose your prices for your own rates (a discount, another tier). Either way the table is used for sessions with no reported cost.
settings.provider.costSource.title: Session costs
settings.provider.defaultEffort.desc: Reasoning effort unless a project overrides it. The levels are the default model's, as the CLI reports them.
settings.provider.defaultEffort.tip: Higher effort is more thorough but slower and uses more tokens.
settings.provider.defaultEffort.title: Default effort
settings.provider.defaultModel.desc: Model for {provider} sessions unless a project overrides it. {provider} default uses its own choice.
settings.provider.defaultModel.tip: Whether your account can use a model is only known when a session starts.
settings.provider.defaultModel.title: Default model
The mode sessions start in unless a project overrides it.
settings.provider.effortFallback.desc: The effort levels offered when {provider} doesn't report a model's own. With the CLI's answer, each model offers just the levels it takes.
settings.provider.effortFallback.tip: The value is what Hive passes to {provider}; the name is what the pickers and footer show.
settings.provider.effortFallback.title: Effort levels (fallback)
settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.co: Recommended only for disposable environments. Each project still has to choose it, and doing so asks for confirmation.
Projects will be able to run sessions where {provider} executes every command, file edit and network request without asking.
{n, plural, one {Enable the {names} option?} other {Enable the {names} options?}}
settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.de: Allow projects and agents to choose {choices}, where the agent runs every action without asking.
settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.ti: {n, plural, one {{names} is never a global default. When turned off, projects and agents using it return to Inherit.} other {{names} are never a global default. When turned off, projects and agents using them return to Inherit.}}
{n, plural, one {Enable the {names} option} other {Enable the {names} options}}
settings.provider.enabled.tip: When off, {provider} agents stay listed but can't start, and Hive doesn't check for its CLI.
settings.provider.enabled.title: Use {provider}
settings.provider.executablePath.desc: Full path to the {provider} CLI ({cli}.exe). Leave empty to detect it automatically.
settings.provider.executablePath.tip: Detection checks PATH and the usual install folders. Copies bundled with editor extensions (VS Code, Cursor…) are never used — Hive requires the standalone CLI.
settings.provider.executablePath.title: CLI path
settings.provider.extraArgs.desc: Additional {cli} command-line arguments for every session.
settings.provider.extraArgs.tip: Projects can add more in their own settings.
settings.provider.extraArgs.title: Extra arguments
settings.provider.modelFallback.desc: Hive asks {provider} which models it has and what each can do. This list is only used when it can't be asked (not installed, too old, or an unexpected answer).
settings.provider.modelFallback.tip: Add, remove and rename models; a custom model ID can still be typed in any model picker. Reset to defaults goes back to Hive's list, which then follows Hive's updates.
settings.provider.modelFallback.title: Models (fallback)
settings.provider.prices.descEstimated: Used to estimate what {provider} sessions would cost at API prices (shown with ≈ on the Overview). USD per million tokens.
settings.provider.prices.descReported: {provider} reports each session's cost itself; these prices are used for sessions without one, or for all of them with Session costs set to your prices. USD per million tokens.
settings.provider.prices.tip: Hive's starting prices are the published ones, checked {checked}: edit any that are out of date, add models and remove them. The table lists the models {provider} has, so a new one shows with "No price" until you enter one. Hive never fetches prices. On a subscription you are not charged these — they show how heavy the work was.
settings.provider.prices.title: API prices
settings.provider.status.tip: Where Hive found {provider}, whether it is signed in and whether an update is available.
settings.provider.status.title: Installation
settings.provider.use200kContext.desc: Run {provider} sessions with a 200K-token context window instead of the model's 1M one, unless a project or agent chooses otherwise. Applies to sessions started afterwards.
settings.provider.use200kContext.tip: Current models have a 1M window at no extra price per token, but a long conversation sends more tokens with every message, and answers slow down as the context fills. With 200K, {provider} compacts the conversation sooner.
settings.provider.use200kContext.title: Use 200K context (instead of 1M)
settings.providerOff.detail: Stop them now, or let them run until they are stopped. Either way no new ones start while it is off.
settings.providerOff.listFailed: Could not list the running agents
settings.providerOff.message: {n, plural, one {An agent is running {provider}: {agents}.} other {# agents are running {provider}: {agents}.}}
settings.providerOff.title: Turn off {provider}?
settings.providers.defaultProvider.desc: The provider Add Agent uses for new agents (one click, with its default settings) unless the project chooses another. Automatic uses the first provider that is turned on and installed (Claude Code, then Codex, then GitHub Copilot).
settings.providers.defaultProvider.tip: Projects can choose their own default in Project Settings. Agents keep the provider they were given; Add Agent… (▾) can choose another.
settings.providers.defaultProvider.title: Default provider
settings.providers.list.desc: Turn on the coding agents you want to use. Agents of a provider that is off stay listed but can't start.
settings.providers.list.tip: Each project agent runs one provider, chosen when you add it (Add Agent) or in its settings. A provider needs its CLI installed and signed in.
settings.providers.list.title: Providers
settings.resetAll.message: Every setting in Settings returns to its default, the advanced settings in advanced.json too. A workspace's own advanced values are kept.
settings.resetAll.title: Reset all settings?
settings.section.advanced.desc: Developer features, the details Hive relies on that a CLI update can break (advanced.json), logs, data and resetting Hive.
settings.section.advanced.label: Advanced
settings.section.agentApi.desc: Local API and built-in MCP server that let agents interact with Hive.
settings.section.agentApi.label: Agent API
settings.section.agents.desc: Defaults for projects running several agents: file locks, new worktrees and merging (projects can override them), and how long background tasks count.
settings.section.agents.label: Agents & Worktrees
settings.section.appearance.label: Appearance
settings.section.assistant.desc: The Hive Assistant's defaults: the side panel's overseer of each workspace (Ctrl+Alt+I). Each workspace can change them in the panel's Assistant Settings.
settings.section.assistant.label: Assistant
settings.section.board.desc: The task board's colours and housekeeping, the same in every workspace.
settings.section.board.label: Board
settings.section.general.label: General
settings.section.keybindings.desc: Change, remove or add shortcuts for any command. Projects can set their own for project and session commands (Project Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts).
settings.section.keybindings.label: Keyboard Shortcuts
settings.section.notifications.desc: Chimes and desktop notifications when agents finish or need you.
settings.section.notifications.label: Notifications
settings.section.provider.desc: The {provider} CLI (the standalone one — copies bundled with editor extensions are not used) and the defaults every project inherits for {provider} agents.
settings.section.providers.desc: The coding agents Hive can run. Turn on the ones you use; each has its own page below with its CLI and the defaults every project inherits.
settings.section.providers.label: Providers
settings.section.sessions.desc: Transcript backups, cache estimates and session behaviour.
settings.section.sessions.label: Sessions
settings.section.updates.desc: Keeping Hive itself up to date. New versions come from Hive's GitHub releases and are verified before they install.
settings.section.updates.label: Updates
settings.section.workspace.desc: The open workspace's card loops, its projects that Hive leaves out (hidden, or removed from Hive with their handovers and cards packed into the folder), and how much Hive keeps for each project.
settings.section.workspace.label: Workspace
settings.sessions.backupRetention.desc: How long Hive keeps its backups of sessions the CLI still has. After that many days without activity they go to the Recycle Bin. A session whose only copy is Hive's backup is never touched.
settings.sessions.backupRetention.tip: Only Hive's own copies go: the CLI's transcript stays, so the session can still be opened and resumed, and what it used stays in the usage history. To remove sessions whose only copy is Hive's, delete them yourself or use Clean Up in Storage.
settings.sessions.backupRetention.title: Keep transcript backups
settings.sessions.backupTranscripts.desc: Copy each session's transcript into the project's .hive/sessions folder.
settings.sessions.backupTranscripts.tip: Agents delete old transcripts after a while (Claude Code: 30 days by default). Backups let you resume and review sessions later. Archived sessions are always preserved.
settings.sessions.cacheTtl.desc: Used to estimate whether resuming a session needs to re-cache its context.
settings.sessions.cacheTtl.tip: Auto detects the cache type from the transcript (5 minutes or 1 hour).
settings.sessions.cacheTtl.title: Prompt cache lifetime
settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.d: Context size, in tokens, at which the context in an agent's pane footer turns orange. Never: it never does.
settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.t: Compacting summarises the conversation so every later message is cheaper; the full history stays in the transcript. Projects can set their own value in Project Settings, and the Assistant has its own (Settings → Assistant). Compact is always available once the agent has finished.
settings.sessions.confirmStop.desc: Ask before stopping a running session.
settings.sessions.confirmStop.tip: Stopped sessions can always be resumed.
settings.sessions.confirmStop.title: Confirm before stopping
settings.sessions.defaultView.desc: How the Session tab shows a project's agents until you choose with its Panes | Tiles toggle.
settings.sessions.defaultView.tip: Panes shows each agent's terminal; Tiles shows each agent as a small tile, so a whole team fits on one screen. A project remembers its own choice once you use its toggle, so changing this only affects projects that haven't chosen yet.
settings.sessions.defaultView.title: Default session view
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.desc: The Sessions tab shows new messages of a running session as they arrive.
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.tip: Off: the transcript shows what was there when you opened it; Refresh loads what is new. You can also switch following on in the viewer itself. The Session tab always shows the agent working.
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.titl: Follow running sessions in the transcript viewer
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.desc: How the Overview and the session lists update while agents work.
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.tip: Live updates as sessions change, at most every 15 seconds and only while the tab is shown. Each update reads the project's session files, so with many sessions or agents a slower choice keeps Hive lighter. Refresh always updates at once.
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.title: Overview updates
settings.sessions.recordPerformance.desc: Count what Hive's Agent API, tools, guidance and skills cost, for the Performance view.
settings.sessions.recordPerformance.tip: Only totals are kept: request and reply sizes, times and outcomes, the size of what each session was given, and the providers' own reported usage. Never prompts, replies, tokens or paths. Kept 30 days per workspace in .hive/metrics (git-ignored, this machine's). Turned off, nothing new is recorded; what was recorded stays until you reset it.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.desc: Clear this workspace's recorded performance metrics.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.tip: Starts the history again from now. Session usage and transcripts are not affected.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.title: Reset performance metrics
settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC: When Hive closed without quitting (a crash, or it was ended), resume the agents that were running when it starts again.
Off: Hive only tells you, with Resume All for you to choose. Either way the notice says when Hive was last seen and which agents were running.
Resume agents after an unexpected close
settings.sessions.tileOrder.desc: The order of the agents' tiles in the Tiles view.
settings.sessions.tileOrder.tip: Same as panes keeps the agents in their panes' order, so a builder stays beside its reviewer: tiles waiting for you or stalled are highlighted where they are, and a page button counts them on other pages. By urgency puts them first, then the agents working, then the idle ones.
settings.sessions.tileOrder.title: Tile order
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.desc: Size, in MB, at which a running conversation's transcript turns orange in its footer and Hive notifies you once.
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.tip: A long conversation slows down the CLI and Hive: each turn, resume and transcript view has more to read. Compacting doesn't shrink the file, which keeps the whole history; handing the work over to a new conversation does (click the size in the footer for Hand Over to…, and choose the agent itself). Projects can set their own value in Project Settings.
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.title: Warn when a transcript is over
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.desc: Forget what the cache holds; a transcript it had is read again when it is next needed. The usage history stays.
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.tip: Only needed if a running session's token counts look wrong. Nothing else is lost: sessions, transcripts, backups and the usage history stay as they are.
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.title: Clear the usage cache
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.desc: How many transcripts Hive keeps the token use of in memory while it runs, so a running session's figures follow each turn without reading it again.
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.tip: What each session used is kept in the usage history, in the workspace's .hive folder: this cache only spares reading a transcript again while Hive runs. The least recently used go first when it is full. {min, number} to {max, number}.
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.title: Usage cache size
settings.token.regenerateMessage: Programs using the current token will stop working. Running sessions pick up the new token when restarted.
settings.updates.checkAutomatically.desc: Look for a new version of Hive shortly after it starts and every 6 hours.
settings.updates.checkAutomatically.tip: When off, Hive only checks when you choose Help → Check for Updates…; development builds never update.
settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.d: Download a new version in the background as soon as it is found.
settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.t: When off, the status bar says a new version is available and you choose when to download it. Downloads are checked against the release checksum.
settings.updates.install.desc: When a downloaded update is installed.
settings.updates.install.tip: Automatically: the update installs when you next quit Hive (never while it is running, so your sessions are not interrupted); Restart and Update installs it straight away. Manually: it installs only when you choose Restart and Update. Either way, Hive asks before stopping agents that are working.
settings.updates.install.title: Install updates
settings.updates.prerelease.desc: Also offer beta versions published before a full release.
settings.updates.prerelease.tip: Pre-releases get new features first and may have rough edges. Turning this off again waits for the next full release rather than going back.
settings.updates.prerelease.title: Include pre-releases
settings.updates.status.tip: The version you are running and the result of the last check.
settings.updates.status.title: Hive Desktop version
settings.usageCache.clearFailed: Could not clear the usage cache
settings.usageCache.clearedDetail: Each transcript is read again the next time it is shown.
settings.viewers.madeDetail: Copy it into the app it is for.
settings.viewers.makeFailed: Could not make the viewer token
settings.viewers.name: Name
settings.viewers.revokeFailed: Could not revoke the viewer token
settings.viewers.revokeMessage: The app using it can no longer read Hive, and its event stream ends now.
settings.workspace.antivirus.desc: Whether Microsoft Defender scans the workspace's folders as Hive's work changes them (builds, tests, git, worktrees), and the exclusions Hive can add for them, with your consent.
settings.workspace.antivirus.tip: Hive checks without administrator rights, so Defender may not show its exclusions (unknown). Adding or removing exclusions asks for administrator rights once. Hive only ever offers these folders: the workspace, its worktrees folder once it exists, and its test area for people developing Hive. It never changes other antivirus products.
settings.workspace.antivirus.title: Antivirus scanning
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.desc: Restore one to bring it back with its cards (and, for a removed one, the handovers packed into its folder). A folder that has left the workspace can be forgotten.
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.tip: Project → Remove Project… hides a project, removes it from Hive (its folder keeps its handovers and cards in .hive/removed, so it can move to another workspace) or deletes it (to the Recycle Bin). Deleted projects are not listed here: restore the folder from the Recycle Bin and Hive sees it as a new project.
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.title: Hidden and removed projects
settings.workspace.loopRounds.desc: How many rounds a card gets in a card loop (a build and its review each) before its agents stop and ask you, when you don't say. Projects can set their own.
settings.workspace.loopRounds.tip: Saying "rounds: 5" when you start a loop still wins. Agents read this when they register the loop (its lane), so a change applies to loops started afterwards.
settings.workspace.loopRounds.title: Card loop rounds
settings.workspace.loopWaitHours.desc: How many hours an agent in a card loop waits with no change before it tells you, when you don't say. Projects can set their own.
settings.workspace.loopWaitHours.tip: Saying "wait: 2h" when you start a loop still wins. Up to a day. Agents read this when they register the loop (its lane), so a change applies to loops started afterwards.
settings.workspace.loopWaitHours.title: Card loop wait
settings.workspace.storage.desc: What Hive keeps for each of the workspace's projects (the biggest first) and the Hive Assistant: transcript backups, archived sessions, attachments and worktrees. Storage opens a project's page, with Clean Up… and Purge…; Purge… here removes everything Hive keeps for the sessions of the whole workspace.
settings.workspace.storage.tip: Measured in the background, a project at a time. The coding agents' own transcripts (in ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.copilot) aren't counted. Hidden projects aren't included.
settings.workspace.storage.title: Storage
